skill.name: browsing-with-playwright
skill.description: Use Playwright MCP to automate browser navigation, form entry, screenshots, page inspection, and web interaction tasks.
skill.summary: Automates browser workflows through a local Playwright MCP server.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown backticks, embedded JSON schema URLs, or local examples. Confirmed risks remain in user-controlled stdio shell execution, arbitrary network-capable MCP transport, predictable /tmp PID files, and unpinned Playwright MCP package execution.

remediation.suggestion: Avoid shell=True for --stdio. Accept an argv array or restrict stdio launches to known MCP server commands.
Pin @playwright/mcp to a reviewed version and document the expected package source before execution.
Use a private runtime directory, validate PID contents, quote substitutions, and avoid following attacker-controlled files.
Require explicit user approval before file uploads, browser_evaluate, browser_run_code, or authenticated workflows.
Default to localhost and warn users before sending headers or tool parameters to a remote MCP endpoint.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Package Execution
semantic_findings.description: scripts/start-server.sh runs npx @playwright/mcp@latest, and SKILL.md shows the same command. This downloads and executes the latest package at runtime.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The helper script and documentation explicitly use @latest through npx. This is a clear supply-chain risk if the package changes or is compromised.

semantic_findings.title: Broad Browser Control Can Expose Data
semantic_findings.description: The documented tools support JavaScript evaluation, Playwright snippets, and local file uploads. Misuse could read sensitive page data or upload local files through a browser session.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The reference documents direct support for evaluating page JavaScript, running Playwright snippets, and uploading absolute local paths. These are powerful capabilities that require explicit trust boundaries.

content.value_statement: Manual browser tasks slow agents when pages need clicks, forms, or screenshots. This skill connects Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to Playwright MCP for controlled browser automation.
actual_capabilities: Start and stop a local Playwright MCP server on a chosen port.
Navigate pages, go back, manage tabs, and resize the browser window.
Capture accessibility snapshots, screenshots, console messages, and network request summaries.
Click, type, select options, drag elements, handle dialogs, and wait for page conditions.
Run JavaScript or Playwright snippets through MCP for complex browser workflows.
List MCP tools and call them over HTTP or stdio using the bundled client.
limitations: It requires Node.js, npx, Python 3, and Playwright browser dependencies.
It can interact only with pages reachable from the local browser environment.
Screenshots alone are not enough for actions; snapshots provide element references.
Browser automation can expose page data or local files if prompts are unsafe.

use_cases.title: Check Web Interfaces
use_cases.description: Run browser steps, capture screenshots, and verify visible page behavior during manual or assisted testing.

use_cases.title: Collect Page Evidence
use_cases.description: Open web pages, inspect snapshots, and gather visible information from sites that require browser rendering.

use_cases.title: Debug User Flows
use_cases.description: Reproduce clicks, form entry, console messages, and network activity while investigating interface issues.

prompt_templates.title: Open a Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Start the Playwright MCP server if needed. Navigate to [URL], take a snapshot, and summarize the visible page state.

prompt_templates.title: Fill a Form
prompt_templates.prompt: Navigate to [URL]. Use a snapshot to find fields, fill them with test data, submit the form, and report the result.

prompt_templates.title: Capture Test Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Open [URL], perform [steps], capture a screenshot, check console messages, and summarize any visible errors.

prompt_templates.title: Automate a Browser Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Playwright MCP to complete [workflow]. Keep actions scoped to trusted pages and explain each state change before continuing.

output_examples.input: Navigate to a product page and capture a full-page screenshot.
output_examples.output: The browser opened the page, verified the main heading, saved a screenshot, and reported the key visible sections.

output_examples.input: Fill a signup form with test data and submit it.
output_examples.output: The form fields were found through a snapshot, filled with test values, submitted, and checked for confirmation text.

output_examples.input: Inspect console errors after opening a dashboard.
output_examples.output: The page loaded in the browser, console messages were reviewed, and error-level messages were summarized for debugging.

best_practices: Use trusted URLs and test accounts when automating authenticated pages.
Take a snapshot before clicking or typing so element references are current.
Stop the Playwright MCP server when browser work is complete.
anti_patterns: Do not upload sensitive local files through browser automation.
Do not run unreviewed browser code snippets from untrusted prompts.
Do not leave a shared browser context running after sensitive sessions.

faq.question: What does this skill automate?
faq.answer: It automates browser actions through Playwright MCP, including navigation, forms, screenshots, snapshots, and page diagnostics.

faq.question: Does it require a local server?
faq.answer: Yes. The helper script starts a local Playwright MCP server, usually on port 8808.

faq.question: Can it scrape pages?
faq.answer: It can extract visible page information from snapshots or browser evaluation when the site permits that access.

faq.question: Can it upload files?
faq.answer: The underlying Playwright MCP tools support file upload, so users should avoid sensitive files.

faq.question: Is it safe for logged-in sites?
faq.answer: Use caution. A shared browser context can retain session state until the server and browser are closed.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
